question: What are Subagents in Claude Code?

options.text: Specialized agents that run in parallel to handle specific tasks
options.explanation: Correct: subagents are Claude agents delegated by the main agent to work on independent tasks in parallel.

options.text: Background processes for running commands
options.explanation: Background processes are shell features. Subagents are full Claude agents with their own context.

options.text: MCP servers for external integrations
options.explanation: MCP servers are external tools. Subagents are built-in Claude Code feature.

options.text: Git branches for parallel development
options.explanation: Git branches are version control, not Claude Code subagents.

options.text: For simple one-line commands like ls or grep
options.explanation: Simple commands do not need subagent overhead — use Bash directly.

options.text: When tasks require different context or expertise
options.explanation: Correct: subagents can specialize in different areas.

options.text: When tasks are independent and can run in parallel
options.explanation: Correct: independent tasks benefit most from parallel execution.

options.text: When tasks depend on each other
options.explanation: Dependent tasks must run sequentially — subagents cannot help here.

question: What context do subagents have access to?

options.text: The results of other subagents
options.explanation: Subagents cannot see each other's results — they work independently.

options.text: Only their specific task description and project files
options.explanation: Correct: subagents work in isolated contexts with only their task and file access.

options.text: The user's direct input
options.explanation: Subagents do not receive direct user input — communication goes through the main agent.

options.text: The full conversation between the user and the main agent
options.explanation: Subagents only receive their specific task description, not the full conversation.

options.text: By running tasks in parallel instead of sequentially
options.explanation: Correct: three 10-minute tasks take ~10 minutes total with subagents, not 30.

options.text: By using a faster model
options.explanation: Subagents use the same model as the main agent.

options.text: By caching results from previous runs
options.explanation: Subagents do not cache results — they run fresh each time.

options.text: By using fewer tokens overall
options.explanation: Subagents may use more tokens due to duplicated context. The benefit is time, not tokens.

question: What happens when subagents complete their tasks?

options.text: Results are discarded after completion
options.explanation: Results are returned to the main agent, not discarded.

options.text: Results are shown directly to the user
options.explanation: Results return to the main agent first, which then presents them to the user.

options.text: Results return to the main agent for aggregation
options.explanation: Correct: the main agent reviews, combines, and presents subagent results.

options.text: Results are saved to files automatically
options.explanation: Subagents can save files, but results also return to the main agent.

question: Which is a good subagent task description?

options.text: Find all endpoints in src/api/ that handle user authentication, and document their request/response formats
options.explanation: Correct: specific scope, clear location, and defined output format.

options.text: Do everything related to the API
options.explanation: Too broad — no clear scope or deliverable.

options.text: Fix all bugs
options.explanation: No scope, no location, no definition of done.

options.text: Look at the API
options.explanation: Too vague — the subagent will waste time figuring out what to do.

question: What is a common mistake when using subagents?

options.text: Creating too many subagents
options.explanation: Correct: overhead and cost outweigh parallelism benefits with too many.

options.text: Creating subagents for sequential tasks
options.explanation: Correct: sequential tasks cannot benefit from parallelism.

options.text: Giving vague task descriptions
options.explanation: Correct: vague descriptions waste subagent time and tokens.

options.text: Not aggregating results
options.explanation: Correct: raw subagent output is not user-friendly without aggregation.

question: How do subagents differ from MCP servers?

options.text: Subagents are for parallel task execution, MCP is for external tool integration
options.explanation: Correct: subagents run tasks within Claude Code, MCP connects to external services.

options.text: Subagents are faster than MCP servers
options.explanation: Speed is not the primary difference — they serve different purposes.

options.text: Subagents are external processes
options.explanation: Subagents run within Claude Code. MCP servers are external processes.

options.text: Subagents use HTTP, MCP uses stdio
options.explanation: Both can use various transports. This is not a distinguishing factor.
